_about: THE ONE PLACE kit says what it ships, and where a service puts it.
Read by tests/staleness.py (--scope templates) and by the
parity-allowlist check in tests/validate.sh. Two consumers, one file:
AGENTS.md's rule is that a property stated in two places is a property
stated in zero times, and the artefact table is exactly the kind of
thing that drifts the moment it is written down twice.
A FIELD IS LOAD-BEARING
id       the name the reporter prints, and the name an allowlist entry
uses. It is a key, not a label: renaming one invalidates every
entry that named it, which is the correct outcome.
source   the path inside the kit checkout. `{lang}` interpolates the
service's DECLARED language (see `languageFrom`).
dest     the path inside the service repo, relative to its root.
bundle   a list of (source, dest) pairs instead of one each. The LGTM
stack is one artefact: docker-compose.yml mounts the other
ten by path, so a service that copies nine of them has a
stack that does not start, and grading the members
separately would call that nine fine copies.
languages which declared languages this artefact applies to. Absent
means every service, including one that has declared no
language at all — an undeclared service still has a
`mise.toml` question to answer.
needsLanguage true when the source path itself is `{lang}`-
interpolated, so the service must DECLARE a language before
the question can be asked at all. It is written out rather
than inferred from the presence of `{lang}` in `source`
because a wrong inference here is the fail-open direction:
the reporter would resolve `{lang}` to a guess and report
the guess as a measurement.
optional true when kit genuinely does not expect universal adoption.
Such an artefact is reported but does not, by itself, make a
service look broken.

artefacts._about_dest: kit's README documents `docker/Dockerfile`, and six of the nine services put theirs at the repository root instead. `destAlternatives` records that rather than leaving it to a human to notice: a path a service legitimately uses is not an absence, and grading a documented, working placement as `absent` is the same class of error as grading a drifted copy as `current` — a report that cries wolf is a report that is muted. The FIRST destination that exists wins, so this never guesses: it is a declared list of paths, resolved by existence, and `absent` still means absent of all of them.

artefacts._about_call: The ONE artefact a service does not copy. It calls the workflow, so a fix in kit reaches every service on the next run with no per-repo PR. `dest: @call` is what tells the reporter to check for a `uses: cafaye/kit/...@<ref>` line rather than for a file — and the check is that the line names the path the file is ACTUALLY at, because GitHub documents that subdirectories of .github/workflows are not supported and a `uses:` line pointing one resolves to nothing at run time.

artefacts._about_bundle: The local stack. It travels as eleven files because docker-compose.yml mounts the other ten by path, so the members are graded as ONE artefact: a service holding eight of them has a stack that will not start, and eleven separately-pinned cells would report that as eight successes and three absences.
